Layout sample: wind met 47% of electricity demand in September

This is a fictional press release written for offline testing of the pipeline. The Sample Energy Agency is not a real organisation and these figures are illustrative.

Wind farms supplied 47% of electricity demand in September 2026, up from 38% in September 2025, the Sample Energy Agency said in its monthly system report published on 3 October 2026.

Total wind generation reached 1,486,000 megawatt hours during the month, the highest monthly output in the agency's records, which began in 2010.

Curtailment, where turbines are switched off because the grid cannot absorb their output, fell to 6% of available wind energy from 9% a year earlier.

The agency cautioned that a single windy month does not establish a trend, and that annual figures for 2026 will be published in January 2027.

Full figures are in the official dataset.
